task.description: Gate the ELIXIR-DEV implementation of ISS-0343 (rescue_missing_schema/1 tolerance for a concurrently-vanished tenant schema in Letflow.EventStore.Registry and Letflow.TenantProvisioning.Backfill) against docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md INV-1..INV-8. Extra concern beyond the usual checklist: whether rescue_missing_schema/1 could mask a genuine cross-tenant isolation bug (e.g. a bug that constructs the wrong schema-qualified query) as a benign 'schema missing, skip it' case.
acceptance_criteria: Scope test run against git diff main...HEAD
Every applicable invariant (INV-1..INV-8) individually verified with PASS/FAIL and how
Explicit answer to the masking-risk question, reasoned from what Postgrex 'undefined_table' actually signals vs. what a real cross-tenant leak looks like
verdict PASS/FAIL with next_action set accordingly

result.summary:
Scope test: diff touches lib/letflow/event_store/registry.ex and lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning/backfill.ex, both of which read/write the tenant-scoped, schema-per-tenant event_type_registry table via Repo prefix: schema_name -- this is a tenant-data path, so INV-1 applies (S1 done, S2 migrations exist per security-invariants.md's 2026-08-17 update). No migration added; no new API route; no response-shaping change; no lookup-by-ID handler added.

INV-1 (tenant data isolation) -- APPLIES, PASS. (a) prefix scoping: every Repo call inside the new/changed code (get_type/2's Repo.one/2, insert_with_monotonicity_check/2's Repo.insert/2, the new fetch_current_max/2's Repo.one/2) still passes prefix: schema_name; schema_name itself is unchanged output of resolve_schema_name/1 (Repo.get_by(Registration, tenant_id: tenant_id) -- untouched by this diff), so no query was moved off :prefix scoping. (b) no migration in this diff -- table creation/reachability unaffected. (c) no tenant_id column touched or newly accepted as a caller-supplied field; rescue_missing_schema/1 and fetch_current_max/2 take only (fun) / (name, schema_name), no tenant_id parameter re-derivation logic added. Confirmed by direct read of the full diff (git diff main...HEAD -- lib/letflow/event_store/registry.ex lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning/backfill.ex) and the surrounding unchanged resolve_schema_name/1.

INV-2, INV-3, INV-5 -- NOT APPLICABLE (S4/S5 not started; no API response-shaping or lookup-by-ID endpoint touched by this diff, consistent with security-invariants.md's applicability note).

INV-4 (secrets by reference only) -- NOT APPLICABLE. No config/env/secret-resolution code touched; grep -rniE for secret-like literals in the two changed files: no hits.

INV-6 (new data-access paths prove scoping) -- satisfied by this handoff itself (this review), same as always.

INV-7 (no SQL string interpolation) -- APPLIES (Ecto in use generally), PASS for this diff specifically: grep -rn 'Repo.query' lib/letflow/event_store/registry.ex lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning/backfill.ex has no hits; every query in the diff is built via Ecto.Query (where/order_by/limit/select) or Repo.one/Repo.insert with a prefix option, never raw SQL.

INV-8 (no unhandled crashes on realistic failure paths) -- APPLIES, PASS -- this diff is, in fact, the fix for an INV-8-shaped gap: a realistic failure path (external I/O -- a Postgres query against a schema that can vanish under a concurrent teardown/offboarding race, i.e. tenant-adjacent operational input, not a supervised per-instance process where a crash is the deliberate design) previously raised an unhandled exception that unwound the whole Enum.reduce_while/3 sweep. The fix replaces it with a typed {:error, :tenant_schema_missing} result threaded through a normal case/with chain -- no bare pattern match that can raise was introduced, and the one new rescue clause narrows to exactly one previously-uncaught crash rather than adding a new one.

Masking-risk question (the acceptance criterion beyond the checklist): rescue_missing_schema/1 cannot mask a cross-tenant isolation bug of the kind INV-1 is about. INV-1's failure mode is a query that reads or writes another tenant's data -- which requires the query to run against a schema that exists (just the wrong one) and succeed. Postgres only raises undefined_table (SQLSTATE 42P01, matched exactly by this helper's rescue clause) when the target relation/schema does not exist at all; a query against a real-but-wrong tenant's existing schema returns that tenant's rows normally, hits no exception, and is therefore never routed through rescue_missing_schema/1 -- there is no code path by which this helper could convert a genuine cross-tenant read into a quiet skip, because a cross-tenant read that succeeds never enters the rescue clause in the first place. Verified this isn't circumvented by construction: schema_name is resolved once, per-call, from resolve_schema_name(tenant_id) (Registration lookup keyed on the tenant_id the caller supplied) -- unchanged by this diff -- so the diff introduces no new path by which a wrong tenant's schema_name could be substituted.

The helper does have a narrower, non-INV-1 residual risk worth naming for REVIEWER: if some *future* bug elsewhere computed a malformed or stale schema_name for the *correct* tenant (a typo, a caching bug, a name-construction regression) such that the resulting schema genuinely does not exist, that bug would also raise undefined_table and get classified as the same 'expected concurrent-teardown race' skip+Logger.warning outcome this fix adds -- turning a hard crash (which today would fail loudly and fast) into a quiet, warning-level skip that could delay detection. This is a diagnosability/availability concern, not a tenant-isolation breach (no tenant's data is exposed to another tenant either way -- the query simply returns nothing, to no one), and it is exactly the risk the design doc (section 2.2) and the implementation both call out explicitly by keeping the rescue narrowly scoped to one exact exception shape, three named call sites, and a log line that includes tenant_id for operator visibility -- it is not a BLOCKER, but flagging it for REVIEWER as a point worth a second look (e.g. whether the warning log should be distinguishable enough from a true concurrent-race pattern if it starts firing for every tenant at once) is appropriate.

No BLOCKER found on any applicable invariant.
